## Ahu Akivi and Puna Pau: how the moai were created and erected

On [Easter Island](/chile/place/easter-island/), monumental stone figures are connected with ancestral remembrance, ceremonial platforms, and the traditions of the Rapa Nui people. To understand their history, it helps to see both **where completed statues were erected** and **where the material for their headpieces was quarried**.

Our approximately **four-hour excursion** combines [Ahu Akivi](/chile/place/ahu-akivi/) and the [Puna Pau quarry](/chile/place/puna-pau-quarry/). It is a compact route through the island's central area; Anakena Beach and the major coastal complexes belong to other itineraries.

## The seven moai of Ahu Akivi

**Seven moai** stand on the platform at Ahu Akivi. The current description notes that they face the ocean, an unusual orientation compared with many other Rapa Nui platforms. In the open landscape, the line of statues stands out against grassy hills and the sky.

A local legend links this group with the first seafarers to arrive on the island. The legend helps explain the site's cultural importance, but does not replace archaeological research or establish a documented history for each figure.

When visiting, look at the statues' positions, their shared alignment, and the way they relate to the landscape. It is a different experience from finding an isolated moai beside a road: the seven figures form a complete ensemble.

## Puna Pau: red stone for the headpieces

At [Puna Pau](/chile/place/puna-pau-quarry/), reddish volcanic tuff was quarried to make **pukao**, large cylindrical elements placed on the heads of some moai. They differ noticeably in color and rock type from the main stone figures.

The quarry shows how complex the craftspeople's work was: separate stone elements had to be carved, transported to the ceremonial platform, and raised onto the statues. The precise ancient transport techniques remain subjects of research, so a single modern reconstruction should not be presented as the only proven explanation.

From a viewpoint on the route, there are views toward the **Hanga Roa** area and coastal bays. The trip therefore combines stoneworking and sculpture with an appreciation of the island's geography.

## How this excursion differs from a full day on Rapa Nui

We offer another itinerary, [Anakena, Rano Raraku and Ahu Tongariki](/chile/easter-island/anakena-rano-raraku-tongariki-tour/), focusing on the major moai quarry, the largest platform with 15 statues, and coastal stops. **Ahu Akivi and Puna Pau** offer a closer look at the ensemble's orientation and the material used for the headpieces.

The guide language, separate price, and included services have not yet been specified for this excursion. When arranging a [Chile tour](/chile/tour/), agree on these details rather than copying the terms of another day on the island.

## Frequently asked questions about Ahu Akivi and Puna Pau

### How many moai are at Ahu Akivi?

There are **seven statues** on the platform, facing the ocean.

### What is the Puna Pau quarry known for?

Reddish volcanic tuff was extracted here for **pukao**, the stone headpieces of the moai.

### How long does the excursion last?

Our excursion takes **approximately four hours**.

### Is Anakena Beach included?

It is not listed in the current itinerary. The beach features in another [Rapa Nui route](/chile/easter-island/anakena-rano-raraku-tongariki-tour/).

## Tours with an Ahu Akivi and Puna Pau excursion on Easter Island

[Ahu Akivi](/chile/place/ahu-akivi/) and [Puna Pau](/chile/place/puna-pau-quarry/) reveal two stages in the making of moai on one excursion: the erected stone figures and the site where red tuff for their headpieces was obtained. We offer this as a [standalone Rapa Nui excursion](/chile/easter-island/ahu-akivi-puna-pau-tour/) lasting approximately four hours.

Our collection includes a [major 14-day tour through Peru, Bolivia, and Chile](/multi-country/tour/south-america-peru-bolivia-chile-easter-island/). Its core route passes through Cusco, Machu Picchu, the Lake Titicaca region, Bolivia and the Uyuni Salt Flat, northern Chile, and Santiago. **Easter Island is listed as an optional three-day, two-night extension.** It is a separate choice to be agreed when creating the itinerary; do not automatically add the island to the mandatory 14 days.

## Two sites and two stages of ancient craftsmanship

At [Ahu Akivi](/chile/place/ahu-akivi/), seven moai stand on a ceremonial platform. Local tradition links them with the arrival of the first Rapa Nui scouts. Their position among grassy slopes helps visitors understand the monument within its landscape, rather than seeing only a row of statues in a photograph.

The [Puna Pau quarry](/chile/place/puna-pau-quarry/) is known for reddish volcanic tuff used to carve cylindrical headpieces called *pukao*. Comparing the two sites helps explain why the stone used for some elements differs from the material of the statues' bodies. Viewpoints around the quarry overlook the Hanga Roa area and coastline.

Unlike excursions to [Rano Raraku](/chile/place/rano-raraku-volcano/) and [Ahu Tongariki](/chile/place/ahu-tongariki/), this route does not focus on the main statue quarry or the great coastal row of moai. Visiting Ahu Akivi and Puna Pau adds an understanding of island technologies and traditions.

| Stop | Main theme |
|---|---|
| Ahu Akivi | Seven moai on a platform |
| Puna Pau | Red tuff and pukao |

## How the excursion fits with Peru, Bolivia, and Chile

The main 14-day itinerary covers a range of elevations and long transfers. In Peru, you visit historic sites in Cusco and Machu Picchu; in Bolivia, you pass through La Paz, Uyuni, and high-altitude lagoons; and in Chile, you explore San Pedro de Atacama and Santiago. Travel pace, tolerance of altitude, and actual connections are important on this route.

[Easter Island](/chile/place/easter-island/) is separate from the mainland stages. The optional island segment includes several independent excursions: monuments on the southern coast, Rano Kau and Orongo, and Ahu Akivi with Puna Pau. Treat it as an additional module with its own flights and overnight stays, not a short stop on the way from Bolivia to Santiago.

Travelers mainly interested in Rapa Nui archaeological sites can consider the [separate three-day Easter Island tour](/chile/tour/easter-island-3-days/). It differs from the extension of the longer route in format and its own itinerary: compare the days on the island, excursion arrangements, accommodation, and flights instead of treating the two products as identical because they share one destination.

## Practical rules for visiting archaeological sites

Rapa Nui National Park requires an admission ticket and an accredited guide to visit archaeological areas. Visitors must stay on permitted paths, keep a safe distance from statues and platforms, and never remove stones or fragments of monuments. These rules are established by the Ma'u Henua community, which manages the park.

For the four-hour excursion, wear comfortable shoes for uneven terrain and bring protection against sun, wind, and brief rain. Before buying flights to the island, check Chile's current tourist entry requirements for Rapa Nui, including trip registration, a return ticket, and proof of accommodation. These formalities apply to the entire island extension even though the archaeological excursion occupies only part of a day.

## Frequently asked questions about tours visiting Ahu Akivi and Puna Pau

### Is Easter Island included in the main 14-day itinerary?

No. In the [Peru, Bolivia and Chile program](/multi-country/tour/south-america-peru-bolivia-chile-easter-island/), the island extension is listed separately as three days and two nights. The inclusions, price, and flights are agreed alongside the main tour.

### How long does the two-site excursion take?

The [Ahu Akivi and Puna Pau excursion](/chile/easter-island/ahu-akivi-puna-pau-tour/) takes approximately four hours. It focuses on two monuments and does not replace an overview of the whole island.

### Is a guide required to visit the monuments?

Yes. Archaeological areas within the national park require an accredited guide and a ticket. Access conditions for individual sites are checked before traveling.

## Ahu Akivi, Puna Pau, and Tahai: four stops in four hours

On [Easter Island](/chile/place/easter-island/), the ancient Rapa Nui culture left more than the famous long rows of stone statues by the ocean. The central and western parts of the island preserve monuments that help explain religious traditions, the origins of stone headpieces, and how ceremonial platforms were built.

Our private itinerary lasts **four hours**. It combines [Ahu Akivi](/chile/place/ahu-akivi/), [Ahu Hanga Pukure](/chile/place/ahu-hanga-poukura/), the [Puna Pau quarry](/chile/place/puna-pau-quarry/), and [Tahai](/chile/place/tahai/). **An English-speaking guide is included**; a Russian-speaking guide is available at additional cost. The excursion price is confirmed for the chosen journey.

## Seven moai at Ahu Akivi

[Ahu Akivi](/chile/place/ahu-akivi/) is known for its restored platform with **seven moai**. Unlike other monuments that travelers see along the shore, this group stands in the island's central area.

Local legend connects these statues with seven explorers said to have been sent by the legendary ruler Hotu Matu'a before the island's main settlement. This cultural story helps explain the site's significance to residents but is not a substitute for archaeological dating.

Look closely at the figures' shapes, the direction they face, and how the platform was constructed. Restored moai reveal the overall design of a ceremonial ensemble, but unrestored sites are equally important to understanding the full history of Rapa Nui.

## Ahu Hanga Pukure: a monument without full restoration

The next stop is [Ahu Hanga Pukure](/chile/place/ahu-hanga-poukura/). Unlike restored Ahu Akivi, it preserves an unrestored ceremonial platform and traces of historical changes.

Such sites remind us that moai have not always stood upright in the familiar postcard arrangements. The island's history included changes in religious practices, crises, and later interventions. The purpose of the visit is to understand the monument in its present condition, not judge it solely by the number of upright statues.

Touching stone elements and moving archaeological finds is forbidden. Park staff determine access to particular areas.

## Puna Pau: red stone for the headpieces

[Puna Pau](/chile/place/puna-pau-quarry/) is a quarry of reddish volcanic tuff. This material was used for the massive moai headpieces often called *pukao*. They differ in color from the statues themselves, which were largely carved from another volcanic tuff around Rano Raraku.

This is a particularly useful stop for anyone wondering how enormous pieces of the statues were made and moved. Here you can see the source of the material and learn about a stage of ancient craftsmanship.

For comparison, a full-day itinerary to the [Rano Raraku quarry](/chile/place/rano-raraku-volcano/) and [Ahu Tongariki](/chile/place/ahu-tongariki/) shows the moai themselves and their ceremonial platforms. But these two attractions **are not included** in the four-hour excursion described here.

## Tahai: three platforms beside the ocean

The itinerary concludes at the [Tahai complex](/chile/place/tahai/). It contains three main ceremonial platforms: **Ko Te Riku**, **Tahai**, and **Vai Uri**. The eyes of the Ko Te Riku statue have been restored, a rare and especially interesting detail when exploring Rapa Nui culture.

The coastal setting reveals the ceremonial structures against the Pacific Ocean. Stay within marked paths and keep away from the platforms. The whole complex is part of Rapa Nui National Park's heritage, recognized by UNESCO.

Travelers interested in monuments from different parts of the island can combine this route with a [full-day excursion along the southern coast and to Anakena Beach](/chile/easter-island/south-coast-moai-anakena-private/). The two complement each other without repeating the main stops.

## Preparing for the four-hour excursion

Even a four-hour visit can involve several exposed sites under strong sun and wind. Bring closed-toe shoes, a hat, water, weather-appropriate clothing, and sun protection. Confirm current national park rules and access to particular monuments before the visit.

The program itself includes **a private excursion with an English-speaking guide**. Transport arrangements, meals, and the cost of the separate outing require clarification; they should not be assumed to be included.

## Frequently asked questions about the Ahu Akivi–Tahai route

### How long does the excursion last?

The stated duration is **four hours**. The itinerary covers four main stops in central and western Rapa Nui.

### How many moai stand at Ahu Akivi?

There are **seven moai** on the restored platform. A legend links them with seven explorers, but it is a tradition rather than a confirmed historical account.

### Can I request a Russian-speaking guide?

Yes, at an additional cost. The base program includes guiding in English.

## Tours featuring Ahu Akivi, Hanga Pukure, Puna Pau, and Tahai

This route combines four archaeological monuments of [Easter Island](/chile/place/easter-island/) in one private excursion: [Ahu Akivi](/chile/place/ahu-akivi/), [Ahu Hanga Pukure](/chile/place/ahu-hanga-poukura/), the [Puna Pau quarry](/chile/place/puna-pau-quarry/), and the [Tahai ceremonial complex](/chile/place/tahai/). We offer this four-hour outing with an English-speaking guide.

The excursion is included in the [three-day tour “Easter Island: Three Days Among Moai and Volcanoes”](/chile/tour/easter-island-3-days/). It takes place on the final day, after breakfast and before the airport transfer. When choosing this trip, consider both the monuments and how much time remains before the return flight.

## Why the four stops are interesting

**[Ahu Akivi](/chile/place/ahu-akivi/).** Seven moai stand on a restored platform in the island's central area. Local legend links them with scouts who arrived on Rapa Nui before the principal settlement.

**[Ahu Hanga Pukure](/chile/place/ahu-hanga-poukura/).** On this itinerary, it is an unrestored platform. It offers an opportunity to compare a monument's preserved condition with restored ensembles, rather than seeing another identical row of fully raised statues.

**[Puna Pau](/chile/place/puna-pau-quarry/).** Red tuff was quarried here for the cylindrical stone headpieces of moai. The quarry explains where the *pukao* came from and how their material differs from the statues' main bodies.

**[Tahai](/chile/place/tahai/).** The coastal complex includes Ko Te Riku, Tahai, and Vai Uri platforms. Ko Te Riku's eyes have been restored, revealing an important detail of the moai's ceremonial appearance.

| Site | What to compare |
|---|---|
| Ahu Akivi | Restored moai |
| Hanga Pukure | Unrestored ahu |
| Puna Pau | Stone used for pukao |
| Tahai | Platforms beside the ocean |

The variety of the monuments makes this an engaging excursion. Discuss the time spent at each stop beforehand, especially if your flight departs the same day.

## How the four monuments fit into the three-day tour

In the [three-day itinerary](/chile/tour/easter-island-3-days/), Day 1 covers the [Rano Kau](/chile/place/rano-kau-volcano/) crater and the Orongo ceremonial village. Day 2 focuses on the southern coast: Ahu Vaihu, Akahanga, the Rano Raraku quarry, Ahu Tongariki, Te Pito Kura, and Anakena Beach. Day 3 concludes the island experience with four sites in central and western Rapa Nui.

The tour lasts **three days and two nights**. It specifies accommodation in a four-star hotel, private excursions with an English-speaking guide, transfers, breakfast on Days 2 and 3, a packed lunch on Day 2, and an admission ticket to the national park. Air tickets, medical insurance, and additional services are listed as excluded. A Russian-speaking guide is possible for a surcharge.

These conditions apply to **this specific three-day tour**. They should not automatically be extended to another excursion with a similar name, even if it also visits Ahu Akivi and Puna Pau.

## Choosing between similar itineraries

The island also offers a [separate “Ahu Akivi and Puna Pau” excursion](/chile/easter-island/ahu-akivi-puna-pau-tour/) lasting about four hours. It focuses on the seven moai and the quarry. The route on this page is broader: it adds Hanga Pukure and Tahai, and is built into the final day of the three-day program.

Another option is the [“Ahu Akivi, Puna Pau and Tahai” excursion](/chile/easter-island/easter-island-akivi-puna-pau-tahai/), without a separate stop at Hanga Pukure. Choose by the actual list of monuments, guiding language, and the excursion's position within the tour's daily schedule, rather than similar-sounding names.

## Tickets, guide, and timing before departure

Rapa Nui National Park requires a valid admission ticket and an accredited guide. At archaeological sites, stay on marked paths, do not touch the moai, and respect the established boundaries. Closed-toe shoes and clothing suitable for sun and wind are recommended for walking.

A morning excursion on departure day requires careful agreement on the finishing time, collection of luggage, and airport transfer. Four hours refers to the excursion; it does not by itself guarantee a connection with every flight. In the [three-day tour](/chile/tour/easter-island-3-days/), the airport transfer follows the archaeological visits.

## Frequently asked questions about the Ahu Akivi–Tahai route

### Which tour includes this private excursion?

It is included on Day 3 of the [three-day Easter Island tour](/chile/tour/easter-island-3-days/), before the flight. It is a standalone excursion module within the itinerary.

### What national park services are included in the three-day tour?

The itinerary includes national park admission and private excursions with an English-speaking guide. Air tickets are excluded; other routes may have different terms.

### Can I replace the English-speaking guide with a Russian-speaking guide?

The published description offers a Russian-speaking guide for an additional charge. Arrange this before booking, alongside the final day's schedule.

## A full day on Rapa Nui: from the quarry to an ocean beach

[Easter Island](/chile/place/easter-island/) is famous for its **moai** statues, but they stand in different parts of the island and offer different experiences. Some remain on quarry slopes, others have been placed on ceremonial platforms, while others fell or were later restored.

Our full-day excursion follows the coast and introduces key stages of this history. The itinerary includes [Ahu Akahanga](/chile/place/ahu-akahanga/), [Rano Raraku](/chile/place/rano-raraku-volcano/), [Ahu Tongariki](/chile/place/ahu-tongariki/), the Poike Peninsula, [Ahu Te Pito Kura](/chile/place/ahu-te-pito-kura/), and [Anakena Beach](/chile/place/anakena-beach/). The return is to [Hanga Roa](/chile/place/hanga-roa/).

## Ahu Akahanga: the legend of the first ruler

The first stop is Ahu Akahanga. Local tradition associates the site with the burial of **Hotu Matu'a**, the island's first king. This is an important part of Rapa Nui oral history, which must be distinguished from an archaeologically proven biography of a historical person.

Such platforms clearly show traces of a long history: fallen and damaged statues, changes to ceremonial places, and the work of researchers. That is why the island's cultural landscape is more than a collection of perfectly preserved monuments.

## Rano Raraku: where the stone figures were carved

[Rano Raraku](/chile/place/rano-raraku-volcano/) is a volcanic quarry associated with the carving of most of the known moai. Numerous figures remain on its slopes at different stages of production, including unfinished statues.

Here you can imagine a statue's journey from stoneworking at the quarry to transport and installation on a ceremonial platform. Not every question about moving the gigantic figures has been conclusively answered, making the visit especially interesting.

## Ahu Tongariki and Te Pito Kura: different scales of monuments

[Ahu Tongariki](/chile/place/ahu-tongariki/) is the island's largest ensemble of restored moai: **15 figures** stand on its platform. This is one of Rapa Nui's most recognizable views. Unlike Rano Raraku, the focus here is on where statues were erected and the layout of a large ceremonial platform.

The route then crosses the **Poike Peninsula** toward [Ahu Te Pito Kura](/chile/place/ahu-te-pito-kura/). Here you learn about the history of one of the island's largest statues. Archaeological sites have distinct histories and should not be evaluated solely by their height.

## Anakena: the final stop by the sea

The last stop is [Anakena Beach](/chile/place/anakena-beach/), where white sand, palms, and turquoise water contrast dramatically with the rocky landscapes of the archaeological sites.

The beach stop comes at the end of the day, but **swimming, beach equipment, and water sports are not separately advertised**. They depend on local conditions and the agreed program. A **packed lunch** is included, so food is provided in that format for this full-day excursion.

## Choosing an island excursion

The Anakena–Rano Raraku–Tongariki itinerary takes **a full day** and visits several major archaeological sites. The [Ahu Akivi–Puna Pau excursion](/chile/easter-island/ahu-akivi-puna-pau-tour/) is shorter, around four hours, and explores the seven moai of Ahu Akivi and the stone used for *pukao* headpieces in more detail.

In both cases, follow the protected area's rules: view monuments from permitted points, do not touch statues, and respect local guides' instructions. The guiding language, separate price, and additional inclusions for the full-day tour are not specified; do not assume them.

## Frequently asked questions about Rano Raraku, Tongariki, and Anakena

### How many moai stand at Ahu Tongariki?

There are **15 restored figures** along the large ceremonial platform.

### Why is Rano Raraku especially important?

It is the quarry where moai were carved; unfinished figures still remain on its slopes.

### Is food included?

A **packed lunch** is included. Other meal services are not provided on this excursion unless agreed separately.

### Can I combine archaeology and the beach in one day?

Yes. The itinerary includes **Anakena** after the archaeological stops, but extra beach activities are not confirmed.
